\fn CameraConfiguration::validate()
 * \brief Validate and possibly adjust the camera configuration
 *
 * This function adjusts the camera configuration to the closest valid
 * configuration and returns the validation status.
 *
 * \todo Define exactly when to return each status code. Should stream
 * parameters set to 0 by the caller be adjusted without returning Adjusted ?
 * This would potentially be useful for applications but would get in the way
 * in Camera::configure(). Do we need an extra status code to signal this ?
 *
 * \todo Handle validation of buffers count when refactoring the buffers API.
 *
 * \return A CameraConfiguration::Status value that describes the validation
 * status.
 * \retval CameraConfiguration::Invalid The configuration is invalid and can't
 * be adjusted. This may only occur in extreme cases such as when the
 * configuration is empty.
 * \retval CameraConfiguration::Adjusted The configuration has been adjusted
 * and is now valid. Parameters may have changed for any stream, and stream
 * configurations may have been removed. The caller shall check the
 * configuration carefully.
 * \retval CameraConfiguration::Valid The configuration was already valid and
 * hasn't been adjusted.
 */

/**
 * \brief Retrieve a reference to a stream configuration

\retval CameraConfiguration::Adjusted The configuration has been adjusted
 * and is now valid. Parameters may have changed for any stream, and stream
 * configurations may have been removed. The caller shall check the
 * configuration carefully.

overview.md/creation/1.text: `Camera::createRequest()`가 반환하는 요청의 소유권은 호출자에게 넘어가며, 호출자가 요청을 삭제해야 합니다.

overview.md/creation/2.text: 같은 요청을 다시 제출하려면 애플리케이션이 먼저 `Request::reuse()`를 호출해 요청 상태를 초기화해야 합니다. 이 함수는 요청과 연결된 상태와 컨트롤을 초기화합니다. 새 요청을 만드는 대신 기존 요청을 재사용할 때는 카메라 큐에 넣기 전에 이 함수를 호출해야 합니다.

overview.md/discovery/1.text: `CameraManager` 인스턴스는 동시에 하나만 존재할 수 있습니다. 기존 인스턴스를 먼저 삭제하지 않고 두 번째 인스턴스를 생성하려고 하면 동작이 정의되지 않습니다.

overview.md/responsibility/0.text: `Camera`는 하나의 이미지 소스에서 하나 이상의 이미지 스트림을 생성할 수 있는 카메라를 나타내며, 장치 설정과 제어 및 이미지 스트림 캡처를 위한 주요 인터페이스를 제공하는 `libcamera`의 중심 객체입니다. `libcamera`는 카메라 인스턴스의 수명을 `std::shared_ptr<>`로 관리하며, 인스턴스는 공유 포인터를 반환하는 `create()` 함수로 생성해야 합니다. `Camera`의 생성자와 소멸자는 비공개이므로 인스턴스를 직접 생성하거나 소멸할 수 없습니다.

camera-model.md/responsibility/0.text: `CameraManager`는 libcamera의 진입점으로, 장치를 열거하고 파이프라인 관리자와 연결하며 애플리케이션에 카메라를 제공합니다. 관리자는 모든 `Camera` 객체를 소유하고 핫플러그와 핫언플러그를 처리해 카메라의 수명을 관리합니다. 애플리케이션은 관리자 인스턴스를 만들고 `start()`를 호출해야 합니다. 관리자는 처음에 정지 상태이며, 시작하면 시스템의 카메라를 열거하여 `list()`와 `get()`으로 접근할 수 있습니다.

camera-model.md/responsibility/1.text: 한 번에 `CameraManager` 인스턴스는 하나만 존재할 수 있으며, 기존 인스턴스를 삭제하기 전에 두 번째 인스턴스를 만들면 동작이 정의되지 않습니다. 카메라는 `std::shared_ptr<>`로 공유되며 마지막 참조가 해제될 때까지 유효합니다. 애플리케이션이 보유한 모든 카메라 참조를 해제한 뒤에는 `stop()`으로 관리자를 정지할 수 있습니다.

camera-model.md/responsibility/2.text: `Camera`는 단일 이미지 소스에서 하나 이상의 이미지 스트림을 생성하는 카메라를 나타내며, 장치 설정과 제어 및 이미지 스트림 캡처의 주 인터페이스를 제공합니다. libcamera는 `std::shared_ptr<>`로 카메라 인스턴스의 수명을 관리하며, 인스턴스는 공유 포인터를 반환하는 `create()`로 생성해야 합니다. `Camera` 생성자와 소멸자는 비공개이므로 인스턴스를 직접 생성하거나 파괴할 수 없습니다.

request-lifecycle.md/resources/4.text: 버퍼에 연결된 펜스가 신호되지 않으면 요청은 타임아웃 후 실패하며, 버퍼에는 펜스가 그대로 남습니다. 애플리케이션은 이 버퍼를 다른 요청에서 재사용하기 전에 `FrameBuffer::releaseFence()`로 펜스를 회수해야 합니다.

request-lifecycle.md/resources/5.text: `Request::reuse()`는 `flags`에 `ReuseBuffers`가 설정된 경우 `bufferMap_`의 각 버퍼에 대해 `buffer->_d()->setRequest(this)`를 호출하여 버퍼를 현재 요청에 연결합니다.

request-lifecycle.md/resources/6.text: `Request::reuse()`는 `flags`에 `ReuseBuffers`가 있으면 `bufferMap_`의 각 기존 버퍼에 현재 요청을 설정한 뒤 그 버퍼를 `pending_`에 추가합니다.

request-lifecycle.md/resources/12.text: 펜스를 사용하는 경우에는 `Request::ReuseBuffers` 플래그를 사용하지 않도록 권고합니다.

catalog/bc46f3612ad5edf8.text: CameraManager는 libcamera의 진입점으로서 장치를 열거하고 파이프라인과 연결하며, 애플리케이션이 시스템의 카메라에 접근할 수 있게 합니다. CameraManager::Private::pipelineFactoryMatch는 팩토리로 PipelineHandler를 반복해서 만들고 장치 열거자와의 매칭을 시도하며, 매칭에 실패하면 반복을 끝냅니다. CameraManager 인스턴스는 동시에 하나만 존재할 수 있습니다. 기존 인스턴스를 먼저 삭제하지 않고 두 번째 인스턴스를 생성하려고 하면 동작이 정의되지 않습니다.

catalog/bc46f3612ad5edf8/en.text: CameraManager is the entry point to libcamera. It enumerates devices, connects them to pipelines, and allows applications to access the system's cameras. CameraManager::Private::pipelineFactoryMatch repeatedly creates PipelineHandler using a factory and attempts to match it with a device enumerator, ending the loop if matching fails. Only one CameraManager instance can exist at a time. Attempting to create a second instance without first deleting the existing instance results in undefined behavior.

 * a time. Attempting to create a second instance without first deleting the
 * existing instance results in undefined behaviour.
 *

 * will enumerate all the cameras present in the system, which can then be
 * listed with list() and retrieved with get().
 *
 * Cameras are shared through std::shared_ptr<>, ensuring that a camera will
 * stay valid until the last reference is released without requiring any special
 * action from the application. Once the application has released all the
 * references it held to cameras, the camera manager can be stopped with

\fn PipelineHandler::match(DeviceEnumerator *enumerator)
 * \brief Match media devices and create camera instances
 * \param[in] enumerator The enumerator providing all media devices found in the
 * system
 *
 * This function is the main entry point of the pipeline handler. It is called
 * by the camera manager with the \a enumerator passed as an argument. It shall
 * acquire from the \a enumerator all the media devices it needs for a single
 * pipeline, create one or multiple Camera instances and register them with the
 * camera manager.
 *
 * If all media devices needed by the pipeline handler are found, they must all
 * be acquired by a call to MediaDevice::acquire(). This function shall then
 * create the corresponding Camera instances, store them internally, and return
 * true. Otherwise it shall not acquire any media device (or shall release all
 * the media devices is has acquired by calling MediaDevice::release()) and
 * return false.
 *
 * If multiple instances of a pipeline are available in the system, the
 * PipelineHandler class will be instantiated once per instance, and its match()
 * function called for every instance. Each call shall acquire media devices for
 * one pipeline instance, until all compatible media devices are exhausted.
 *
 * If this function returns true, a new instance of the pipeline handler will
 * be created and its match() function called.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return true if media devices have been acquired and camera instances
 * created, or false otherwise
 */

findings.claim_quote: `PipelineHandler::match()`는 `CameraManager` 스레드에서 호출되며, `true`를 반환하면 새 `PipelineHandler` 인스턴스가 생성되고 그 인스턴스의 `match()`가 호출됩니다.

\brief Queue a request to the camera
 * \param[in] request The request to queue to the camera
 *
 * This function queues a \a request to the camera for capture.
 *
 * After allocating the request with createRequest(), the application shall
 * fill it with at least one capture buffer before queuing it. Requests that
 * contain no buffers are invalid and are rejected without being queued.
 *
 * Once the request has been queued, the camera will notify its completion
 * through the \ref requestCompleted signal.
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -ENODEV The camera has been disconnected from the system
 * \retval -EACCES The camera is not running so requests can't be queued
 * \retval -EXDEV The request does not belong to this camera
 * \retval -EINVAL The request is invalid
 * \retval -ENOMEM No buffer memory was available to handle the request
 */
int Camera::queueRequest

\brief Create a request object for the camera
 * \param[in] cookie Opaque cookie for application use
 *
 * This function creates an empty request for the application to fill with
 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.
 *
 * The \a cookie is stored in the request and is accessible through the
 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.
 *
 * The ownership of the returned request is passed to the caller, which is
 * responsible for deleting it. The request may be deleted in the completion
 * handler, or reused after resetting its state with Request::reuse().
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Configured or Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return A pointer to the newly created request, or nullptr on error
 */
std::unique_ptr<Request> Camera::createRequest(uint64_t cookie)

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

findings.claim_quote: `Request::addBuffer()`는 요청에 버퍼의 참조를 저장합니다. 호출자는 요청 완료 콜백이 호출될 때까지 버퍼가 유효하게 유지되도록 해야 합니다.

findings.condition: 완료된 요청에 대해 호출하며, 큐 앞 요청이 대기 중이면 반복을 중단합니다.
findings.actor: 파이프라인 핸들러가 completeRequest를 호출하고 카메라가 requestComplete를 통해 통지합니다.
findings.timing: 호출은 CameraManager 스레드에서 이루어지고, 함수 반환 후 핸들러는 해당 요청에 접근하면 안 됩니다. 호출 순서는 자유롭지만 반환 순서는 제출 순서입니다.
findings.scope: completeRequest의 API 계약과 큐 분기이며, 함수 호출 스레드 자체가 애플리케이션 콜백 실행 스레드의 별도 보장을 뜻하지는 않습니다.
findings.reason: 대상과 한영 비교 문장은 호출 의무, 반환 후 접근 금지, 호출과 반환 순서의 구분 및 큐 분기를 유지합니다. 출처는 중단 시 취소에도 같은 완료 규칙을 적용합니다.

\brief Signal request completion
 * \param[in] request The request that has completed
 *
 * The pipeline handler shall call this function to notify the \a camera that
 * the request has completed. The request is no longer managed by the pipeline
 * handler and shall not be accessed once this function returns.
 *
 * This function ensures that requests will be returned to the application in
 * submission order, the pipeline handler may call it on any complete request
 * without any ordering constraint.
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 */
void PipelineHandler::completeRequest

findings.claim_quote: 파이프라인 핸들러는 `completeRequest()`를 `CameraManager` 스레드에서 호출해야 하며, 함수가 반환된 뒤에는 해당 요청에 접근해서는 안 됩니다. 이 함수는 완료된 요청을 순서에 관계없이 호출받을 수 있으며, 요청을 제출 순서대로 애플리케이션에 반환합니다. 조사 계획에서는 호출 문맥과 별도로 대기열 앞 요청의 상태를 확인합니다. 상태가 `Request::RequestPending`이면 반복문을 빠져나가고, 그렇지 않으면 해당 요청을 대기열에서 꺼내 `camera->requestComplete(req)`를 호출하는 다음 분기를 확인합니다.

\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer(Request *request, FrameBuffer *buffer)
{
	Camera *camera = request->_d()->camera();
	camera->bufferCompleted.emit(request, buffer);
	return request->_d()->completeBuffer(buffer);
}

sources.source_quote:
An application needs to perform a sequence of operations on a camera before
 * it is ready to process requests. The camera needs to be acquired and
 * configured to prepare the camera for capture. Once started the camera can
 * process requests until it is stopped. When an application is done with a
 * camera, the camera needs to be released.

An application may start and stop a camera multiple times as long as it is
 * not released. The camera may also be reconfigured.

Functions that affect the camera state as defined below are generally not
 * synchronized with each other by the Camera class. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring their synchronization if necessary.

\fn PipelineHandler::match(DeviceEnumerator *enumerator)
 * \brief Match media devices and create camera instances
 * \param[in] enumerator The enumerator providing all media devices found in the
 * system
 *
 * This function is the main entry point of the pipeline handler. It is called
 * by the camera manager with the \a enumerator passed as an argument. It shall
 * acquire from the \a enumerator all the media devices it needs for a single
 * pipeline, create one or multiple Camera instances and register them with the
 * camera manager.
 *
 * If all media devices needed by the pipeline handler are found, they must all
 * be acquired by a call to MediaDevice::acquire(). This function shall then
 * create the corresponding Camera instances, store them internally, and return
 * true. Otherwise it shall not acquire any media device (or shall release all
 * the media devices is has acquired by calling MediaDevice::release()) and
 * return false.
 *
 * If multiple instances of a pipeline are available in the system, the
 * PipelineHandler class will be instantiated once per instance, and its match()
 * function called for every instance. Each call shall acquire media devices for
 * one pipeline instance, until all compatible media devices are exhausted.
 *
 * If this function returns true, a new instance of the pipeline handler will
 * be created and its match() function called.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return true if media devices have been acquired and camera instances
 * created, or false otherwise
 */

findings.claim_quote: 애플리케이션은 촬영을 준비하기 위해 카메라를 확보하고 구성한 뒤 시작해야 하며, 시작된 카메라는 정지할 때까지 요청을 처리할 수 있고, 애플리케이션은 사용을 마치면 카메라를 해제해야 합니다. 애플리케이션은 카메라를 해제하지 않은 동안 여러 번 시작하고 정지할 수 있으며, 카메라를 재구성할 수도 있습니다. sources.source_quote:
An application needs to perform a sequence of operations on a camera before
 * it is ready to process requests. The camera needs to be acquired and
 * configured to prepare the camera for capture. Once started the camera can
 * process requests until it is stopped. When an application is done with a
 * camera, the camera needs to be released.

An application may start and stop a camera multiple times as long as it is
 * not released. The camera may also be reconfigured.

Functions that affect the camera state as defined below are generally not
 * synchronized with each other by the Camera class. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring their synchronization if necessary.

\fn PipelineHandler::match(DeviceEnumerator *enumerator)
 * \brief Match media devices and create camera instances
 * \param[in] enumerator The enumerator providing all media devices found in the
 * system
 *
 * This function is the main entry point of the pipeline handler. It is called
 * by the camera manager with the \a enumerator passed as an argument. It shall
 * acquire from the \a enumerator all the media devices it needs for a single
 * pipeline, create one or multiple Camera instances and register them with the
 * camera manager.
 *
 * If all media devices needed by the pipeline handler are found, they must all
 * be acquired by a call to MediaDevice::acquire(). This function shall then
 * create the corresponding Camera instances, store them internally, and return
 * true. Otherwise it shall not acquire any media device (or shall release all
 * the media devices is has acquired by calling MediaDevice::release()) and
 * return false.
 *
 * If multiple instances of a pipeline are available in the system, the
 * PipelineHandler class will be instantiated once per instance, and its match()
 * function called for every instance. Each call shall acquire media devices for
 * one pipeline instance, until all compatible media devices are exhausted.
 *
 * If this function returns true, a new instance of the pipeline handler will
 * be created and its match() function called.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return true if media devices have been acquired and camera instances
 * created, or false otherwise
 */

findings.claim_quote: To prepare for capture, the application must acquire and configure the camera, then start it. Once started, the camera can process requests until it is stopped, and the application must release the camera when it has finished using it. While the camera remains acquired, the application can start and stop it multiple times and can also reconfigure it. The Camera class generally does not synchronize functions that affect the camera state with one another, so the caller must ensure synchronization of these functions when necessary. When an implementer of match for new hardware has acquired all the media devices required for a pipeline, the implementer must create one or more Camera instances, store them internally, and register them with the camera manager.

findings.condition: Success requires all media devices needed for one pipeline to be found and acquired; otherwise no devices remain acquired.
findings.actor: The PipelineHandler::match() implementer acquires or releases devices and creates, stores and registers cameras; the camera manager invokes match.
findings.timing: match runs on the CameraManager thread. A true return leads to creation of a new handler instance and another match call.
findings.scope: Success and failure obligations for a single pipeline match and the subsequent repeat behavior; the English peer covers the successful creation and registration subset.
findings.reason: The stated acquisition, release, return, registration, thread and repetition requirements agree with the source. The English peer does not contradict the additional failure-path obligations.

findings.claim_quote: If the PipelineHandler::match() implementer finds all media devices required for a single pipeline, it must acquire each device using MediaDevice::acquire(), create and internally store one or more corresponding Camera instances, register them with the camera manager, and then return true. If the PipelineHandler::match() implementer cannot find all required media devices, it must not acquire any media devices if it has not yet acquired any; if it has already acquired some, it must release all acquired devices using MediaDevice::release() and return false. \fn PipelineHandler::generateConfiguration()
 * \brief Generate a camera configuration for a specified camera
 * \param[in] camera The camera to generate a default configuration for
 * \param[in] roles A list of stream roles
 *
 * Generate a default configuration for the \a camera for a specified list of
 * stream roles. The caller shall populate the \a roles with the use-cases it
 * wishes to fetch the default configuration for. The returned configuration
 * can then be examined by the caller to learn about the selected streams and
 * their default parameters.
 *
 * The intended companion to this is \a configure() which can be used to change
 * the group of streams parameters.
 *
 * \context This function may be called from any thread and shall be
 * \threadsafe. It shall not modify the state of the \a camera in the pipeline
 * handler.

 * \return A valid CameraConfiguration if the requested roles can be satisfied,
 * or a null pointer otherwise.
 */

findings.claim_quote: generateConfiguration 호출자는 기본 구성을 가져오려는 사용 사례를 roles에 채워야 합니다. generateConfiguration()이 반환하는 구성에서 호출자는 선택된 스트림 집합과 각 스트림의 기본 파라미터를 확인할 수 있습니다. generateConfiguration()은 요청된 roles를 충족할 수 있으면 유효한 CameraConfiguration을 반환해야 하며, 그렇지 않으면 null 포인터를 반환해야 합니다. PipelineHandler::generateConfiguration()은 어떤 스레드에서든 호출될 수 있으며, 구현은 스레드 안전성을 갖춰야 합니다.

\fn PipelineHandler::configure()
 * \brief Configure a group of streams for capture
 * \param[in] camera The camera to configure
 * \param[in] config The camera configurations to setup
 *
 * Configure the specified group of streams for \a camera according to the
 * configuration specified in \a config. The intended caller of this interface

 * The configuration is guaranteed to have been validated with

 * not perform further validation and may rely on any custom field stored in its

 * instance to each StreamConfiguration entry in the CameraConfiguration using

 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 */

\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer

\brief Signal request completion

 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.

 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request

 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.

 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the

 * be left unmodified.

 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.

\brief Queue a request to the camera
 * \param[in] request The request to queue to the camera
 *
 * This function queues a \a request to the camera for capture.
 *
 * After allocating the request with createRequest(), the application shall
 * fill it with at least one capture buffer before queuing it. Requests that
 * contain no buffers are invalid and are rejected without being queued.
 *
 * Once the request has been queued, the camera will notify its completion
 * through the \ref requestCompleted signal.
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -ENODEV The camera has been disconnected from the system
 * \retval -EACCES The camera is not running so requests can't be queued
 * \retval -EXDEV The request does not belong to this camera
 * \retval -EINVAL The request is invalid
 * \retval -ENOMEM No buffer memory was available to handle the request
 */
int Camera::queueRequest

\brief Create a request object for the camera
 * \param[in] cookie Opaque cookie for application use
 *
 * This function creates an empty request for the application to fill with
 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.
 *
 * The \a cookie is stored in the request and is accessible through the
 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.

 * handler, or reused after resetting its state with Request::reuse().

findings.timing: Completion is signaled after queuing; the front request and queue size are checked while processing the waiting queue.
findings.scope: The claim summarizes the API completion-notification contract and the supplied queue-processing path, not device processing success or callback execution thread.

findings.claim_quote: If Camera::queueRequest returns 0, the request was successfully queued. After the request is queued, the camera signals its completion with requestCompleted. waitingRequests_ holds requests waiting to become ready; if the request at the front is not ready, it does not forward subsequent requests to the device. maxQueuedRequestsDevice_ is the limit on the number of requests queued to the device. \fn PipelineHandler::queueRequestDevice()
 * \brief Queue a request to the device
 * \param[in] camera The camera to queue the request to
 * \param[in] request The request to queue
 *
 * This function queues a capture request to the device for processing. The
 * request contains a set of buffers associated with streams and a set of
 * parameters. The pipeline handler shall program the device to ensure that the
 * parameters will be applied to the frames captured in the buffers provided in
 * the request.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 */

\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer(Request *request, FrameBuffer *buffer)

findings.claim_quote: 함수 이름은 PipelineHandler::queueRequestDevice()이며, 성공 시 0을 반환합니다. 오류가 발생하면 음수 오류 코드를 반환합니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 요청의 버퍼 완료를 알리기 위해 CameraManager 스레드에서 completeBuffer()를 호출해야 합니다. 마지막 버퍼가 완료되어도 요청은 자동으로 완료되지 않으므로 completeRequest()를 명시적으로 호출해야 합니다.

findings.condition: Applies to device-queue success or error and completion of a buffer belonging to a request.
findings.actor: The pipeline handler signals buffer and request completion.
findings.timing: completeBuffer() is called on the CameraManager thread; request completion remains explicit after the last buffer completes.
findings.scope: The source contract covers queueRequestDevice() return values and the buffer and request completion duties.
findings.reason: The English claim preserves the Korean claim's obligations and matches the source, including the distinction between buffer and request completion.

\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed

 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer

findings.claim_quote: Even when the last buffer completes, the request does not complete automatically, so the pipeline handler must explicitly complete the request by calling completeRequest(). After marking the request as complete, completeRequest checks requests starting from the front of queuedRequests_. If the status of the request at the front is RequestPending, the function stops iterating and does not check the requests behind it. Otherwise, the function verifies that no buffers are pending, removes the request from the queue, and calls requestComplete() to return the request to the application in submission order.

\brief Create a request object for the camera
 * \param[in] cookie Opaque cookie for application use
 *
 * This function creates an empty request for the application to fill with
 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.
 *
 * The \a cookie is stored in the request and is accessible through the
 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.
 *
 * The ownership of the returned request is passed to the caller, which is
 * responsible for deleting it. The request may be deleted in the completion
 * handler, or reused after resetting its state with Request::reuse().
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Configured or Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return A pointer to the newly created request, or nullptr on error
 */
std::unique_ptr<Request> Camera::createRequest(uint64_t cookie)

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

findings.claim_quote: Camera::createRequest()가 반환한 요청의 소유권은 호출자에게 넘어가며, 호출자는 요청을 삭제할 책임이 있습니다. 호출자는 완료 핸들러에서 요청을 삭제하거나 Request::reuse()로 상태를 초기화한 뒤 재사용할 수 있습니다. Request::addBuffer()는 요청에 버퍼의 참조를 저장합니다. 호출자는 요청 완료 콜백이 호출될 때까지 버퍼가 유효하게 유지되도록 해야 합니다.

findings.condition: Applies to the created request and a buffer added to it.
findings.actor: The caller owns and must delete the request, and is responsible for keeping the buffer valid.
findings.timing: The request may be deleted in the completion handler or reused after reset; the buffer must remain valid until the request completion callback is called.
findings.scope: The API contract covers request ownership and the lifetime of the referenced buffer.
findings.reason: The translation preserves the ownership, permission to delete or reuse, and buffer-lifetime obligation supported by the sources.

findings.claim_quote: Ownership of the request returned by Camera::createRequest() passes to the caller, who is responsible for deleting it. The caller may delete the request in the completion handler or reset its state with Request::reuse() and reuse it. Request::addBuffer() stores a reference to the buffer in the request. The caller must ensure that the buffer remains valid until the request completion callback is called.

findings.condition: 완료된 요청에 completeRequest()를 호출하며, 큐 앞의 요청이 pending이면 반복을 중단한다.
findings.actor: 파이프라인 핸들러가 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출하고 카메라가 요청 완료를 통지한다.
findings.timing: 함수 반환 후 요청에 접근하지 않으며, 호출 순서와 애플리케이션 반환 순서는 별개다.
findings.scope: completeRequest()의 API 보장과 큐 처리 분기이며 콜백 실행 스레드에 대한 주장은 아니다.
findings.reason: 원문과 번역이 호출 의무, 접근 금지, 반환 순서 및 분기를 일치하게 서술한다. 버퍼 완료와 요청 완료를 구분하는 관련 주장과도 양립한다.
findings.claim_quote: 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeRequest()를 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 하며, 함수가 반환된 뒤에는 해당 요청에 접근해서는 안 됩니다. 이 함수는 완료된 요청을 순서에 관계없이 호출받을 수 있으며, 요청을 제출 순서대로 애플리케이션에 반환합니다. 조사 계획에서는 호출 문맥과 별도로 대기열 앞 요청의 상태를 확인합니다. 상태가 Request::RequestPending이면 반복문을 빠져나가고, 그렇지 않으면 해당 요청을 대기열에서 꺼내 camera->requestComplete(req)를 호출하는 다음 분기를 확인합니다.

findings.claim_quote: The pipeline handler must call completeRequest() on the CameraManager thread and must not access the request after the function returns. This function may be called with completed requests in any order and returns requests to the application in submission order. The investigation plan checks the status of the request at the front of the queue separately from the calling context. If the status is Request::RequestPending, the loop exits; otherwise, the plan checks the next branch, which removes the request from the queue and calls camera->requestComplete(req).

findings.reason: 원문과 번역은 검사 조건과 신호 보장을 충실히 반영하고 관련 큐잉 주장과 일치한다. 생략된 activeStreams_의 수신자는 해당 함수와 소스에서 명확하다.
findings.claim_quote: Camera::queueRequest()는 앞선 카메라 상태, 요청의 생성 카메라, 요청 상태와 제어 목록 검사를 통과한 뒤 request->buffers()가 비어 있으면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 요청의 각 버퍼에 연결된 stream을 activeStreams_.find(stream)으로 찾고, 결과가 activeStreams_.end()와 같으면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 요청을 카메라에 큐잉하는 데 성공하면 0을 반환하며, 이 반환이 촬영 완료를 뜻하지는 않습니다. 요청이 큐잉된 후 카메라는 requestCompleted 신호로 완료를 알립니다.

findings.claim_quote: Camera::queueRequest() returns -EINVAL if request->buffers() is empty after passing the preceding checks of the camera state, the camera that created the request, the request state, and the control list. Camera::queueRequest() uses activeStreams_.find(stream) to find the stream associated with each buffer in the request and returns -EINVAL if the result equals activeStreams_.end(). Camera::queueRequest() returns 0 if it successfully queues the request to the camera; this return value does not mean that capture is complete. After the request is queued, the camera signals completion with requestCompleted.

findings.condition: 요청 생성과 파이프라인 핸들러의 큐 등록 과정에 적용됩니다.
findings.actor: 파이프라인 핸들러가 등록하고, 연결된 콜백이 doQueueRequests를 호출합니다.
findings.timing: 생성 시 등록하고 준비 신호에 따라 콜백이 호출됩니다.
findings.scope: 요청이 가리키는 카메라의 대기 목록과 해당 요청의 준비 호출입니다.
findings.reason: 등록 시점과 콜백, 대기 목록의 객체 및 300ms 인자가 소스와 일치합니다. 영문 번역도 같은 계약을 서술하며, 관련 동료 주장의 큐 처리 설명과 충돌하지 않습니다.
findings.claim_quote: PipelineHandler::registerRequest()는 요청이 생성될 때 호출되며, 파이프라인 핸들러가 해당 요청에 필요한 일회성 초기화를 수행할 기회를 제공합니다. PipelineHandler::registerRequest()가 prepared 신호에 연결한 콜백은 doQueueRequests()를 호출합니다. PipelineHandler::queueRequest는 요청이 가리키는 카메라의 내부 목록 waitingRequests_에 request를 추가합니다. PipelineHandler::queueRequest는 prepare 호출에 시간 인자로 300ms, 즉 300밀리초를 전달합니다.

findings.condition: 요청 생성과 파이프라인 핸들러의 큐 등록 과정에 적용됩니다.
findings.actor: 파이프라인 핸들러가 등록하고, 연결된 콜백이 doQueueRequests를 호출합니다.
findings.timing: 생성 시 등록하고 준비 신호에 따라 콜백이 호출됩니다.
findings.scope: 요청이 가리키는 카메라의 대기 목록과 해당 요청의 준비 호출입니다.
findings.reason: 영문 주장은 한국어와 동일한 등록, 콜백, 대기 목록 및 시간 인자를 나타내며 소스와 일치합니다. 관련 동료 주장의 큐 처리 설명과도 충돌하지 않습니다.
findings.claim_quote: PipelineHandler::registerRequest() is called when a request is created, giving the pipeline handler an opportunity to perform one-time initialization required for that request. The callback that PipelineHandler::registerRequest() connected to the prepared signal calls doQueueRequests(). PipelineHandler::queueRequest adds request to waitingRequests_, the internal list of the camera referenced by the request. PipelineHandler::queueRequest passes 300ms, or 300 milliseconds, as the time argument in the call to prepare.

findings.condition: 완료된 요청에 대한 completeRequest의 계약입니다.
findings.actor: 파이프라인 핸들러가 함수를 호출하며 반환 후 해당 요청에 접근하지 않아야 합니다.
findings.timing: 접근 금지는 함수 반환 후 적용되고, 애플리케이션 반환은 제출 순서를 따릅니다.
findings.scope: 완료 함수 호출 순서와 애플리케이션에 요청이 반환되는 순서는 별개입니다.
findings.reason: 소스는 관리 종료와 반환 후 접근 금지, 완료 요청에 대한 순서 제약 없는 호출, 제출 순서에 따른 반환을 명시합니다. 버퍼 완료와 명시적 요청 완료를 구별하는 동료 주장 및 대기열 처리 설명과도 양립합니다.

sources.source_quote:
This function ensures that requests will be returned to the application in
 * submission order, the pipeline handler may call it on any complete request
 * without any ordering constraint.

\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer(Request *request, FrameBuffer *buffer)

findings.claim_quote: 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeRequest가 반환한 뒤 해당 요청에 접근해서는 안 됩니다. 해당 요청은 더 이상 파이프라인 핸들러가 관리하지 않습니다. completeRequest는 요청이 제출 순서대로 애플리케이션에 반환되도록 합니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 완료된 요청에 대해 순서 제약 없이 completeRequest를 호출할 수 있습니다.

findings.condition: The ordering permission applies to completed requests passed to completeRequest.
findings.actor: The pipeline handler calls completeRequest and must not access the request after it returns; the function ensures the return order.
findings.timing: Calls may occur in any order, while requests are returned to the application in submission order. The access prohibition applies after the function returns.
findings.scope: The claim summarizes the completeRequest API contract; it does not assert a callback execution thread or transfer of ownership.
findings.reason: The source supports the management, access and ordering statements. The relevant peers describe the same return-order guarantee and the queue processing that implements it; they do not impose an ordering constraint on calls.

sources.source_quote:
This function ensures that requests will be returned to the application in

findings.claim_quote: The pipeline handler must not access the request after completeRequest returns. The pipeline handler no longer manages the request. completeRequest ensures that requests are returned to the application in submission order. The pipeline handler may call completeRequest for completed requests without any ordering constraints.

findings.condition: 큐가 비어 있지 않고 맨 앞 요청이 RequestPending인 경우 반복을 중단합니다. 대기 요청의 실제 전달은 준비 상태와 장치 큐 한도에 따릅니다.
findings.actor: 파이프라인 핸들러가 완료 함수를 호출하며 cancelRequest는 해당 요청을 취소합니다.
findings.timing: completeRequest는 반복문 뒤에 doQueueRequests를 호출하고, cancelRequest는 취소 후 completeRequest를 호출합니다.
findings.scope: CameraManager 스레드 의무는 두 완료 함수의 호출 문맥에 관한 것이며 콜백 실행 스레드를 보장하지 않습니다.
findings.reason: 소스의 분기, 함수 호출 순서와 스레드 의무가 주장과 일치합니다. 관련 한영 피어의 버퍼 완료 및 요청 완료 설명도 양립합니다.
findings.claim_quote: PipelineHandler::completeRequest()의 while 루프는 큐 맨 앞 요청의 상태가 Request::RequestPending이면 break를 실행해 루프를 중단합니다. PipelineHandler::completeRequest()는 대기 중인 요청을 파이프라인에 큐잉할 수 있도록 마지막에 doQueueRequests(camera)를 호출합니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeBuffer와 completeRequest를 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다. PipelineHandler::cancelRequest()는 먼저 request->_d()->cancel()을 호출한 다음 completeRequest(request)를 호출합니다.

findings.condition: The loop breaks when the nonempty queue's front request is RequestPending; forwarding waiting requests remains subject to readiness and the device queue limit.
findings.actor: The pipeline handler calls the completion functions; cancelRequest cancels the specified request.
findings.timing: completeRequest calls doQueueRequests after the loop, and cancelRequest calls completeRequest after cancellation.
findings.scope: The CameraManager thread obligation applies to invocation of the two completion functions and does not establish the callback execution thread.
findings.reason: The source supports the branch, call sequence and thread obligation. The Korean counterpart and relevant completion peers are consistent with these claims.
findings.claim_quote: The while loop in PipelineHandler::completeRequest() executes break and exits the loop if the status of the request at the front of the queue is Request::RequestPending. PipelineHandler::completeRequest() calls doQueueRequests(camera) at the end so that pending requests can be queued to the pipeline. The pipeline handler must call completeBuffer and completeRequest on the CameraManager thread. PipelineHandler::cancelRequest() first calls request->_d()->cancel() and then calls completeRequest(request).

findings.condition: 버퍼 완료 통지와 마지막 버퍼 완료 후의 요청 완료에 적용됩니다.
findings.actor: 파이프라인 핸들러가 두 완료 함수를 호출합니다.
findings.timing: 두 함수의 호출은 CameraManager 스레드에서 이루어져야 합니다. 마지막 버퍼 완료만으로 요청이 자동 완료되지는 않습니다.
findings.scope: completeBuffer의 통지와 추적 결과, 반환값 및 completeRequest의 명시적 호출에 관한 소스 계약입니다.
findings.reason: 소스는 반환값의 양쪽 의미와 별도 완료 의무를 뒷받침합니다. 영문 번역과 관련 피어도 이 내용에 부합합니다. 호출 스레드 요건은 콜백 실행 스레드에 대한 주장이 아닙니다.
findings.claim_quote: 조사 계획으로, 파이프라인 핸들러가 completeBuffer를 호출할 때 버퍼 완료 알림과 요청의 버퍼 추적 결과를 확인합니다. 반환값이 true이면 요청의 모든 버퍼가 완료된 것이고, false이면 그렇지 않습니다. 마지막 버퍼가 완료되어도 요청은 자동으로 완료되지 않으므로, 파이프라인 핸들러가 completeRequest를 별도로 호출하는지 확인합니다. 두 함수는 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다.

findings.condition: Applies to buffer completion notification and request completion after the last buffer completes.
findings.actor: The pipeline handler calls both completion functions.
findings.timing: Both calls must occur on the CameraManager thread; completion of the last buffer alone does not automatically complete the request.
findings.scope: The source contract covers completeBuffer notification, tracking and return value, and explicit completeRequest invocation.
findings.reason: The source supports both return-value cases and the separate completion obligation. The Korean claim and relevant peers agree. The calling-thread requirement does not assert a callback execution thread.
findings.claim_quote: The investigation plan is to check the buffer completion notification and the request's buffer tracking result when the pipeline handler calls completeBuffer. If the function returns true, all buffers in the request are complete; if the function returns false, they are not. Because the request does not complete automatically when the last buffer completes, the plan also checks whether the pipeline handler calls completeRequest separately. Both functions must be called on the CameraManager thread.

catalog/cc13337248296521.text: 애플리케이션은 촬영을 준비하기 위해 카메라를 확보하고 구성한 뒤 시작해야 하며, 시작된 카메라는 정지할 때까지 요청을 처리할 수 있고, 애플리케이션은 사용을 마치면 카메라를 해제해야 합니다. 애플리케이션은 카메라를 해제하지 않은 동안 여러 번 시작하고 정지할 수 있으며, 카메라를 재구성할 수도 있습니다. Camera 클래스는 카메라 상태에 영향을 주는 함수들을 일반적으로 서로 동기화하지 않으므로, 필요한 경우 호출자가 이 함수들의 동기화를 책임져야 합니다. 새 하드웨어의 match 구현자는 하나의 파이프라인에 필요한 미디어 장치를 모두 확보한 경우 하나 이상의 Camera 인스턴스를 생성하고 내부에 저장하며 카메라 관리자에 등록해야 합니다.

catalog/cc13337248296521/en.text: To prepare for capture, the application must acquire and configure the camera, then start it. Once started, the camera can process requests until it is stopped, and the application must release the camera when it has finished using it. While the camera remains acquired, the application can start and stop it multiple times and can also reconfigure it. The Camera class generally does not synchronize functions that affect the camera state with one another, so the caller must ensure synchronization of these functions when necessary. When an implementer of match for new hardware has acquired all the media devices required for a pipeline, the implementer must create one or more Camera instances, store them internally, and register them with the camera manager.

PipelineHandler::match() 구현자는 필요한 미디어 장치를 모두 찾지 못한 경우 아직 장치를 확보하지 않았다면 어떤 미디어 장치도 확보해서는 안 되며, 이미 일부를 확보했다면 확보한 장치를 모두 MediaDevice::release()로 해제하고 false를 반환해야 합니다. catalog/2b8257a13828a079/en.text: The caller of generateConfiguration must populate roles with the use case for which it wants to obtain the default configuration. catalog/abc6bfb712c37be9.text: PipelineHandler::configure() 구현자는 카메라를 구성할 때 StreamConfiguration::setStream()을 사용해 CameraConfiguration의 각 StreamConfiguration 항목에 Stream 인스턴스를 연결해야 합니다. PipelineHandler::configure()는 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출되며, 구현은 성공하면 0을 반환하고 실패하면 음수 오류 코드를 반환해야 합니다.

catalog/abc6bfb712c37be9/en.text: When configuring a camera, the PipelineHandler::configure() implementer must use StreamConfiguration::setStream() to associate a Stream instance with each StreamConfiguration entry in CameraConfiguration. catalog/1627ee523ce59b5e.text: queueRequestDevice 구현자는 스트림에 연결된 버퍼 집합과 파라미터 집합을 담은 요청을 처리할 때, 요청에 제공된 버퍼에 캡처된 프레임에 해당 파라미터가 적용되도록 장치를 설정해야 합니다. queueRequestDevice 구현자는 성공하면 0을, 실패하면 음수 오류 코드를 반환해야 합니다. PipelineHandler::queueRequestDevice()는 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출됩니다.

catalog/1627ee523ce59b5e/en.text: When processing a request containing a set of buffers associated with streams and a set of parameters, the queueRequestDevice implementer must configure the device so that the parameters are applied to frames captured into the buffers provided in the request. catalog/8c98cf06e9a737ea.text: 파이프라인 핸들러는 요청의 버퍼 완료를 알리기 위해 CameraManager 스레드에서 completeBuffer()를 호출해야 합니다. 이 함수는 애플리케이션에 버퍼 완료를 통지하고 요청 내부의 버퍼 추적 정보를 갱신합니다. 마지막 버퍼를 완료해도 요청 전체가 자동으로 완료되는 것은 아닙니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeBuffer로 버퍼 완료를 알리고, 요청은 completeRequest를 명시적으로 호출해 완료해야 합니다.

catalog/8c98cf06e9a737ea/en.text: The pipeline handler must call completeBuffer() on the CameraManager thread to signal the completion of a buffer in the request. Completing the last buffer does not automatically complete the entire request. catalog/1db2d36b239cc850.text: createIPA 내부 람다는 isSignatureValid(m)이 참이면 T::Threaded 프록시 객체를 생성하고, 거짓이면 T::Isolated 프록시 객체를 생성합니다. createIPA는 생성한 프록시의 isValid 검사가 실패하면 오류를 기록하고 nullptr을 반환합니다. createIPA는 생성한 프록시가 유효성 검사를 통과하면 해당 프록시를 반환합니다.

catalog/3f9cc2d54c6ee372.text: 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeRequest가 반환된 뒤에는 더 이상 관리하지 않는 해당 요청에 접근해서는 안 됩니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 완료된 요청을 순서 제약 없이 completeRequest에 전달할 수 있으며, 이 함수는 요청을 제출 순서대로 애플리케이션에 반환합니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeRequest를 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다.

catalog/3f9cc2d54c6ee372/en.text: The pipeline handler must not access the corresponding request after completeRequest has returned, because the pipeline handler no longer manages it. The pipeline handler can pass completed requests to completeRequest without any ordering constraints, and this function returns the requests to the application in submission order. catalog/cf09f7c08436100c.text: 애플리케이션은 createRequest()로 할당한 요청을 Camera::queueRequest()에 전달하기 전에 최소 한 개의 캡처 버퍼로 채워야 하며, 버퍼가 없는 요청은 유효하지 않아 큐에 들어가지 않고 거부됩니다. Camera::queueRequest()로 큐에 넣은 요청의 처리가 완료되면 카메라는 requestCompleted 신호로 애플리케이션에 알립니다. 호출자는 카메라가 Running 상태일 때만 Camera::queueRequest()를 호출해야 합니다.

catalog/cf09f7c08436100c/en.text: The application must populate a request allocated with createRequest() with at least one capture buffer before passing it to Camera::queueRequest(). The caller must call Camera::queueRequest() only when the camera is in the Running state.

catalog/1b80b85a4247e633.text: Camera 상태를 바꾸는 함수를 호출하는 호출자는 필요한 경우 함수 간 동기화를 보장해야 합니다. 호출자는 PipelineHandler::completeRequest()를 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다.

catalog/1b80b85a4247e633/en.text: Callers invoking functions that change the Camera state must ensure synchronization between the functions when necessary. Callers must call PipelineHandler::completeRequest() on the CameraManager thread.

catalog/5376f4ccfbc77ab6.text: Camera::start는 isAccessAllowed에 허용 상태 값으로 Private::CameraConfigured를 전달합니다. Camera::start의 호출자는 카메라 상태에 영향을 주는 다른 함수와 이 호출을 동기화해야 합니다. 문서화 대상은 카메라 시작 타이밍입니다.

catalog/5376f4ccfbc77ab6/en.text: Camera::start passes Private::CameraConfigured to isAccessAllowed as the allowed state value. The caller of Camera::start must synchronize this call with other functions that affect the camera state. The timing of camera startup is to be documented.

catalog/3d37fab169d774b1.text: 호출자는 카메라가 Configured 상태일 때만 Camera::start를 호출할 수 있습니다. 카메라 상태에 영향을 주는 함수들은 일반적으로 Camera 클래스에서 서로 동기화하지 않습니다. 호출자는 필요한 경우 이 함수들을 동기화해야 합니다.

catalog/3d37fab169d774b1/en.text: The caller can call Camera::start only when the camera is in the Configured state. Functions that affect the camera state are generally not synchronized with one another in the Camera class. The caller must synchronize these functions when necessary.

catalog/885073788254d1b3.text: Camera::createRequest()는 스레드 안전 함수입니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 스레드 안전 함수입니다. 이 함수는 카메라가 Running 상태일 때만 호출할 수 있습니다. 호출자는 Camera::start와 Camera::stop을 각각 카메라 상태에 영향을 주는 다른 함수와 동기화해야 합니다.

catalog/885073788254d1b3/en.text: Camera::createRequest() is a thread-safe function. Camera::queueRequest() is a thread-safe function. This function can be called only when the camera is in the Running state. The caller must synchronize Camera::start and Camera::stop each with other functions that affect the camera state.

catalog/bae5175c944593b3.text: 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeBuffer()와 completeRequest()를 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다. cancelRequest()에는 completeRequest()와 같은 규칙이 적용됩니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 요청이 완료되면 Camera::requestComplete를 호출해 카메라에 알립니다. Camera::requestComplete는 requestCompleted.emit(request)를 호출해 완료된 요청을 애플리케이션에 알리는 신호를 발행합니다.

catalog/0ec721dd2951522e.text: Camera::queueRequest가 0을 반환하면 요청을 큐에 넣는 데 성공했음을 의미합니다. 요청이 큐에 들어간 후 카메라는 requestCompleted 신호로 완료를 알립니다. waitingRequests_는 준비를 기다리는 요청을 보관하며, 맨 앞 요청이 준비되지 않으면 뒤의 요청도 장치로 전달하지 않습니다. maxQueuedRequestsDevice_는 장치에 큐잉된 요청 수의 한도로, queuedRequests_의 크기가 이 값과 같으면 대기 요청의 전달을 중단합니다.

catalog/0ec721dd2951522e/en.text: If Camera::queueRequest returns 0, the request was successfully queued. After the request is queued, the camera signals its completion with requestCompleted. waitingRequests_ holds requests waiting to become ready; if the request at the front is not ready, it does not forward subsequent requests to the device. maxQueuedRequestsDevice_ is the limit on the number of requests queued to the device. catalog/99d6fb26203f2ec8.text: 함수 이름은 PipelineHandler::queueRequestDevice()이며, 성공 시 0을 반환합니다. 오류가 발생하면 음수 오류 코드를 반환합니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 요청의 버퍼 완료를 알리기 위해 CameraManager 스레드에서 completeBuffer()를 호출해야 합니다. 마지막 버퍼가 완료되어도 요청은 자동으로 완료되지 않으므로 completeRequest()를 명시적으로 호출해야 합니다.

catalog/99d6fb26203f2ec8/en.text: The function is named PipelineHandler::queueRequestDevice() and returns 0 on success. If an error occurs, the function returns a negative error code. The pipeline handler must call completeBuffer() on the CameraManager thread to signal completion of a buffer in the request. Even when the last buffer is completed, the request is not completed automatically, so the pipeline handler must explicitly call completeRequest().

catalog/5570030e70a8758a.text: 마지막 버퍼가 완료되어도 요청은 자동으로 완료되지 않으므로, 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeRequest()를 호출하여 요청을 명시적으로 완료해야 합니다. completeRequest는 완료된 요청을 표시한 뒤 queuedRequests_의 맨 앞부터 확인합니다. 맨 앞 요청의 상태가 RequestPending이면 반복을 중단하므로 그 뒤의 요청은 확인하지 않습니다. 그렇지 않으면 대기 중인 버퍼가 없음을 확인하고 해당 요청을 큐에서 제거한 뒤 requestComplete()를 호출하여 애플리케이션에 제출 순서대로 반환합니다.

catalog/5570030e70a8758a/en.text: Even when the last buffer completes, the request does not complete automatically, so the pipeline handler must explicitly complete the request by calling completeRequest(). After marking the request as complete, completeRequest checks requests starting from the front of queuedRequests_. If the status of the request at the front is RequestPending, the function stops iterating and does not check the requests behind it. Otherwise, the function verifies that no buffers are pending, removes the request from the queue, and calls requestComplete() to return the request to the application in submission order.

catalog/17213e255910fe0b.text: Camera::createRequest()가 반환한 요청의 소유권은 호출자에게 넘어가며, 호출자는 요청을 삭제할 책임이 있습니다. 호출자는 완료 핸들러에서 요청을 삭제하거나 Request::reuse()로 상태를 초기화한 뒤 재사용할 수 있습니다. Request::addBuffer()는 요청에 버퍼의 참조를 저장합니다. 호출자는 요청 완료 콜백이 호출될 때까지 버퍼가 유효하게 유지되도록 해야 합니다.

catalog/17213e255910fe0b/en.text: Ownership of the request returned by Camera::createRequest() passes to the caller, who is responsible for deleting it. The caller may delete the request in the completion handler or reset its state with Request::reuse() and reuse it. Request::addBuffer() stores a reference to the buffer in the request. The caller must ensure that the buffer remains valid until the request completion callback is called.

catalog/ffb688343bad5630.text: 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeRequest()를 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 하며, 함수가 반환된 뒤에는 해당 요청에 접근해서는 안 됩니다. 이 함수는 완료된 요청을 순서에 관계없이 호출받을 수 있으며, 요청을 제출 순서대로 애플리케이션에 반환합니다. 조사 계획에서는 호출 문맥과 별도로 대기열 앞 요청의 상태를 확인합니다. 상태가 Request::RequestPending이면 반복문을 빠져나가고, 그렇지 않으면 해당 요청을 대기열에서 꺼내 camera->requestComplete(req)를 호출하는 다음 분기를 확인합니다.

catalog/ffb688343bad5630/en.text: The pipeline handler must call completeRequest() on the CameraManager thread and must not access the request after the function returns. This function may be called with completed requests in any order and returns requests to the application in submission order. The investigation plan checks the status of the request at the front of the queue separately from the calling context. If the status is Request::RequestPending, the loop exits; otherwise, the plan checks the next branch, which removes the request from the queue and calls camera->requestComplete(req).

catalog/0f876f3d920cfff8.text: Camera::queueRequest()는 앞선 카메라 상태, 요청의 생성 카메라, 요청 상태와 제어 목록 검사를 통과한 뒤 request->buffers()가 비어 있으면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 요청의 각 버퍼에 연결된 stream을 activeStreams_.find(stream)으로 찾고, 결과가 activeStreams_.end()와 같으면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 요청을 카메라에 큐잉하는 데 성공하면 0을 반환하며, 이 반환이 촬영 완료를 뜻하지는 않습니다. 요청이 큐잉된 후 카메라는 requestCompleted 신호로 완료를 알립니다.

catalog/0f876f3d920cfff8/en.text: Camera::queueRequest() returns -EINVAL if request->buffers() is empty after passing the preceding checks of the camera state, the camera that created the request, the request state, and the control list. Camera::queueRequest() uses activeStreams_.find(stream) to find the stream associated with each buffer in the request and returns -EINVAL if the result equals activeStreams_.end(). Camera::queueRequest() returns 0 if it successfully queues the request to the camera; this return value does not mean that capture is complete. After the request is queued, the camera signals completion with requestCompleted.

catalog/e9bb20c903920914.text: Request::addBuffer()는 요청에 버퍼의 참조를 저장합니다. 호출자는 요청 완료 콜백이 호출될 때까지 버퍼가 유효하게 유지되도록 해야 합니다. Request::addBuffer()가 성공하면 유효한 Fence의 소유권이 buffer로 이동합니다. Request::addBuffer()가 실패하면 전달받은 fence의 소유권을 가져가지 않고 변경하지 않은 상태로 남깁니다.

catalog/e9bb20c903920914/en.text: Request::addBuffer() stores a reference to the buffer in the request. The caller must ensure that the buffer remains valid until the request completion callback is invoked. If Request::addBuffer() succeeds, ownership of the valid Fence is transferred to buffer. If Request::addBuffer() fails, it does not take ownership of the supplied fence and leaves it unchanged.

catalog/f5cd6c61f3810f88.text: PipelineHandler::registerRequest()는 요청이 생성될 때 호출되며, 파이프라인 핸들러가 해당 요청에 필요한 일회성 초기화를 수행할 기회를 제공합니다. PipelineHandler::registerRequest()가 prepared 신호에 연결한 콜백은 doQueueRequests()를 호출합니다. PipelineHandler::queueRequest는 요청이 가리키는 카메라의 내부 목록 waitingRequests_에 request를 추가합니다. PipelineHandler::queueRequest는 prepare 호출에 시간 인자로 300ms, 즉 300밀리초를 전달합니다.

catalog/f5cd6c61f3810f88/en.text: PipelineHandler::registerRequest() is called when a request is created, giving the pipeline handler an opportunity to perform one-time initialization required for that request. The callback that PipelineHandler::registerRequest() connected to the prepared signal calls doQueueRequests(). \brief Signal request completion
 * \param[in] request The request that has completed
 *
 * The pipeline handler shall call this function to notify the \a camera that
 * the request has completed. The request is no longer managed by the pipeline
 * handler and shall not be accessed once this function returns.

 * This function ensures that requests will be returned to the application in
 * submission order, the pipeline handler may call it on any complete request
 * without any ordering constraint.

 * This function is the main entry point of the pipeline handler. It is called

 * one pipeline instance, until all compatible media devices are exhausted.
 *
 * If this function returns true, a new instance of the pipeline handler will
 * be created and its match() function called.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return true if media devices have been acquired and camera instances

 */

\brief Queue a request to the camera
 * \param[in] request The request to queue to the camera
 *
 * This function queues a \a request to the camera for capture.
 *
 * After allocating the request with createRequest(), the application shall
 * fill it with at least one capture buffer before queuing it. Requests that
 * contain no buffers are invalid and are rejected without being queued.
 *
 * Once the request has been queued, the camera will notify its completion
 * through the \ref requestCompleted signal.
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -ENODEV The camera has been disconnected from the system
 * \retval -EACCES The camera is not running so requests can't be queued
 * \retval -EXDEV The request does not belong to this camera
 * \retval -EINVAL The request is invalid
 * \retval -ENOMEM No buffer memory was available to handle the request
 */

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()

 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream

\fn PipelineHandler::generateConfiguration()
 * \brief Generate a camera configuration for a specified camera
 * \param[in] camera The camera to generate a default configuration for
 * \param[in] roles A list of stream roles
 *
 * Generate a default configuration for the \a camera for a specified list of
 * stream roles. The caller shall populate the \a roles with the use-cases it
 * wishes to fetch the default configuration for. The returned configuration
 * can then be examined by the caller to learn about the selected streams and
 * their default parameters.
 *
 * The intended companion to this is \a configure() which can be used to change
 * the group of streams parameters.
 *
 * \context This function may be called from any thread and shall be
 * \threadsafe. It shall not modify the state of the \a camera in the pipeline
 * handler.
 *
 * \return A valid CameraConfiguration if the requested roles can be satisfied,
 * or a null pointer otherwise.
 */

\fn PipelineHandler::configure()
 * \brief Configure a group of streams for capture
 * \param[in] camera The camera to configure
 * \param[in] config The camera configurations to setup
 *
 * Configure the specified group of streams for \a camera according to the
 * configuration specified in \a config. The intended caller of this interface
 * is the Camera class which will receive configuration to apply from the
 * application.
 *
 * The configuration is guaranteed to have been validated with
 * CameraConfiguration::validate(). The pipeline handler implementation shall
 * not perform further validation and may rely on any custom field stored in its
 * custom CameraConfiguration derived class.
 *
 * When configuring the camera the pipeline handler shall associate a Stream
 * instance to each StreamConfiguration entry in the CameraConfiguration using
 * the StreamConfiguration::setStream() function.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 */

\fn PipelineHandler::queueRequestDevice()
 * \brief Queue a request to the device
 * \param[in] camera The camera to queue the request to
 * \param[in] request The request to queue
 *
 * This function queues a capture request to the device for processing. The
 * request contains a set of buffers associated with streams and a set of
 * parameters. The pipeline handler shall program the device to ensure that the
 * parameters will be applied to the frames captured in the buffers provided in
 * the request.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 */

\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer

\brief Signal request completion
 * \param[in] request The request that has completed
 *
 * The pipeline handler shall call this function to notify the \a camera that
 * the request has completed. The request is no longer managed by the pipeline
 * handler and shall not be accessed once this function returns.
 *
 * This function ensures that requests will be returned to the application in
 * submission order, the pipeline handler may call it on any complete request
 * without any ordering constraint.
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 */
void PipelineHandler::completeRequest

\brief Signal request completion
 * \param[in] request The request that has completed
 *
 * The pipeline handler shall call this function to notify the \a camera that
 * the request has completed. The request is no longer managed by the pipeline
 * handler and shall not be accessed once this function returns.
 *
 * This function ensures that requests will be returned to the application in
 * submission order, the pipeline handler may call it on any complete request
 * without any ordering constraint.
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 */
void PipelineHandler::completeRequest

\brief Queue a request to the camera
 * \param[in] request The request to queue to the camera
 *
 * This function queues a \a request to the camera for capture.
 *
 * After allocating the request with createRequest(), the application shall
 * fill it with at least one capture buffer before queuing it. Requests that
 * contain no buffers are invalid and are rejected without being queued.
 *
 * Once the request has been queued, the camera will notify its completion
 * through the \ref requestCompleted signal.
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -ENODEV The camera has been disconnected from the system
 * \retval -EACCES The camera is not running so requests can't be queued
 * \retval -EXDEV The request does not belong to this camera
 * \retval -EINVAL The request is invalid
 * \retval -ENOMEM No buffer memory was available to handle the request
 */
int Camera::queueRequest

\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer

\brief Start capture from camera
 * \param[in] controls Controls to be applied before starting the Camera
 *
 * Start the camera capture session, optionally providing a list of controls to
 * apply before starting. Once the camera is started the application can queue
 * requests to the camera to process and return to the application until the
 * capture session is terminated with \a stop().

 * \context This function may only be called when the camera is in the

 * synchronized by the caller with other functions that affect the camera
 * state.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -ENODEV The camera has been disconnected from the system
 * \retval -EACCES The camera is not in a state where it can be started
 */
int Camera::start

\brief Create a request object for the camera
 * \param[in] cookie Opaque cookie for application use
 *
 * This function creates an empty request for the application to fill with
 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.
 *
 * The \a cookie is stored in the request and is accessible through the
 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.
 *
 * The ownership of the returned request is passed to the caller, which is
 * responsible for deleting it. The request may be deleted in the completion
 * handler, or reused after resetting its state with Request::reuse().
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Configured or Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return A pointer to the newly created request, or nullptr on error
 */
std::unique_ptr<Request> Camera::createRequest(uint64_t cookie)

\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer

\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer(Request *request, FrameBuffer *buffer)

\brief Signal request completion
 * \param[in] request The request that has completed
 *
 * The pipeline handler shall call this function to notify the \a camera that
 * the request has completed. The request is no longer managed by the pipeline
 * handler and shall not be accessed once this function returns.
 *
 * This function ensures that requests will be returned to the application in
 * submission order, the pipeline handler may call it on any complete request
 * without any ordering constraint.
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 */
void PipelineHandler::completeRequest

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

\brief Signal request completion
 * \param[in] request The request that has completed
 *
 * The pipeline handler shall call this function to notify the \a camera that
 * the request has completed. The request is no longer managed by the pipeline
 * handler and shall not be accessed once this function returns.
 *
 * This function ensures that requests will be returned to the application in
 * submission order, the pipeline handler may call it on any complete request
 * without any ordering constraint.
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 */
void PipelineHandler::completeRequest

\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer(Request *request, FrameBuffer *buffer)
{
	Camera *camera = request->_d()->camera();
	camera->bufferCompleted.emit(request, buffer);
	return request->_d()->completeBuffer(buffer);
}
