sources.source_quote:
An application needs to perform a sequence of operations on a camera before
 * it is ready to process requests. The camera needs to be acquired and
 * configured to prepare the camera for capture. Once started the camera can
 * process requests until it is stopped. When an application is done with a
 * camera, the camera needs to be released.

An application may start and stop a camera multiple times as long as it is
 * not released. The camera may also be reconfigured.

Functions that affect the camera state as defined below are generally not
 * synchronized with each other by the Camera class. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring their synchronization if necessary.

\fn PipelineHandler::match(DeviceEnumerator *enumerator)
 * \brief Match media devices and create camera instances
 * \param[in] enumerator The enumerator providing all media devices found in the
 * system
 *
 * This function is the main entry point of the pipeline handler. It is called
 * by the camera manager with the \a enumerator passed as an argument. It shall
 * acquire from the \a enumerator all the media devices it needs for a single
 * pipeline, create one or multiple Camera instances and register them with the
 * camera manager.
 *
 * If all media devices needed by the pipeline handler are found, they must all
 * be acquired by a call to MediaDevice::acquire(). This function shall then
 * create the corresponding Camera instances, store them internally, and return
 * true. Otherwise it shall not acquire any media device (or shall release all
 * the media devices is has acquired by calling MediaDevice::release()) and
 * return false.
 *
 * If multiple instances of a pipeline are available in the system, the
 * PipelineHandler class will be instantiated once per instance, and its match()
 * function called for every instance. Each call shall acquire media devices for
 * one pipeline instance, until all compatible media devices are exhausted.
 *
 * If this function returns true, a new instance of the pipeline handler will
 * be created and its match() function called.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return true if media devices have been acquired and camera instances
 * created, or false otherwise
 */

findings.claim_quote: 애플리케이션은 촬영을 준비하기 위해 카메라를 확보하고 구성한 뒤 시작해야 하며, 시작된 카메라는 정지할 때까지 요청을 처리할 수 있고, 애플리케이션은 사용을 마치면 카메라를 해제해야 합니다. 애플리케이션은 카메라를 해제하지 않은 동안 여러 번 시작하고 정지할 수 있으며, 카메라를 재구성할 수도 있습니다. Camera 클래스는 카메라 상태에 영향을 주는 함수들을 일반적으로 서로 동기화하지 않으므로, 필요한 경우 호출자가 이 함수들의 동기화를 책임져야 합니다. 새 하드웨어의 match 구현자는 하나의 파이프라인에 필요한 미디어 장치를 모두 확보한 경우 하나 이상의 Camera 인스턴스를 생성하고 내부에 저장하며 카메라 관리자에 등록해야 합니다.

findings.condition: 카메라가 확보된 상태에서 시작·정지와 재구성이 가능하며, match는 필요한 장치를 확보한 경우에 적용됩니다.
findings.actor: 애플리케이션, 동기화 책임이 있는 호출자, match 구현자의 역할을 구분합니다.
findings.timing: 카메라 준비와 시작 후 요청을 처리하고, 사용을 마치면 해제합니다.
findings.scope: 카메라 수명 주기, 호출자 동기화 의무 및 match의 생성·등록 계약입니다.
findings.reason: 영어 문장은 한국어 주장과 같은 의무와 가능성을 표현하며 해당 소스의 계약과 일치합니다. 상세 match 주장과 분석 표현의 한계도 양립합니다.

findings.claim_quote: To prepare for capture, the application must acquire and configure the camera, then start it. Once started, the camera can process requests until it is stopped, and the application must release the camera when it has finished using it. While the camera remains acquired, the application can start and stop it multiple times and can also reconfigure it. The Camera class generally does not synchronize functions that affect the camera state with one another, so the caller must ensure synchronization of these functions when necessary. When an implementer of match for new hardware has acquired all the media devices required for a pipeline, the implementer must create one or more Camera instances, store them internally, and register them with the camera manager.

\fn PipelineHandler::generateConfiguration()
 * \brief Generate a camera configuration for a specified camera
 * \param[in] camera The camera to generate a default configuration for
 * \param[in] roles A list of stream roles
 *
 * Generate a default configuration for the \a camera for a specified list of
 * stream roles. The caller shall populate the \a roles with the use-cases it
 * wishes to fetch the default configuration for. The returned configuration
 * can then be examined by the caller to learn about the selected streams and
 * their default parameters.
 *
 * The intended companion to this is \a configure() which can be used to change
 * the group of streams parameters.
 *
 * \context This function may be called from any thread and shall be
 * \threadsafe. It shall not modify the state of the \a camera in the pipeline
 * handler.
 *
 * \return A valid CameraConfiguration if the requested roles can be satisfied,
 * or a null pointer otherwise.
 */

findings.claim_quote: generateConfiguration 호출자는 기본 구성을 가져오려는 사용 사례를 roles에 채워야 합니다. generateConfiguration()이 반환하는 구성에서 호출자는 선택된 스트림 집합과 각 스트림의 기본 파라미터를 확인할 수 있습니다. generateConfiguration()은 요청된 roles를 충족할 수 있으면 유효한 CameraConfiguration을 반환해야 하며, 그렇지 않으면 null 포인터를 반환해야 합니다. PipelineHandler::generateConfiguration()은 어떤 스레드에서든 호출될 수 있으며, 구현은 스레드 안전성을 갖춰야 합니다.

\fn PipelineHandler::configure()
 * \brief Configure a group of streams for capture
 * \param[in] camera The camera to configure
 * \param[in] config The camera configurations to setup
 *
 * Configure the specified group of streams for \a camera according to the
 * configuration specified in \a config. The intended caller of this interface
 * is the Camera class which will receive configuration to apply from the
 * application.
 *
 * The configuration is guaranteed to have been validated with
 * CameraConfiguration::validate(). The pipeline handler implementation shall
 * not perform further validation and may rely on any custom field stored in its
 * custom CameraConfiguration derived class.

 * instance to each StreamConfiguration entry in the CameraConfiguration using
 * the StreamConfiguration::setStream() function.

 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 */

\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer

\brief Signal request completion
 * \param[in] request The request that has completed
 *
 * The pipeline handler shall call this function to notify the \a camera that
 * the request has completed. The request is no longer managed by the pipeline
 * handler and shall not be accessed once this function returns.
 *
 * This function ensures that requests will be returned to the application in
 * submission order, the pipeline handler may call it on any complete request
 * without any ordering constraint.
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 */
void PipelineHandler::completeRequest

\brief Signal request completion
 * \param[in] request The request that has completed
 *
 * The pipeline handler shall call this function to notify the \a camera that
 * the request has completed. The request is no longer managed by the pipeline
 * handler and shall not be accessed once this function returns.
 *
 * This function ensures that requests will be returned to the application in
 * submission order, the pipeline handler may call it on any complete request
 * without any ordering constraint.
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 */
void PipelineHandler::completeRequest

\brief Queue a request to the camera
 * \param[in] request The request to queue to the camera
 *
 * This function queues a \a request to the camera for capture.
 *
 * After allocating the request with createRequest(), the application shall
 * fill it with at least one capture buffer before queuing it. Requests that
 * contain no buffers are invalid and are rejected without being queued.
 *
 * Once the request has been queued, the camera will notify its completion
 * through the \ref requestCompleted signal.
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -ENODEV The camera has been disconnected from the system
 * \retval -EACCES The camera is not running so requests can't be queued
 * \retval -EXDEV The request does not belong to this camera
 * \retval -EINVAL The request is invalid
 * \retval -ENOMEM No buffer memory was available to handle the request
 */
int Camera::queueRequest

\brief Queue a request to the camera
 * \param[in] request The request to queue to the camera
 *
 * This function queues a \a request to the camera for capture.
 *
 * After allocating the request with createRequest(), the application shall
 * fill it with at least one capture buffer before queuing it. Requests that
 * contain no buffers are invalid and are rejected without being queued.
 *
 * Once the request has been queued, the camera will notify its completion
 * through the \ref requestCompleted signal.
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -ENODEV The camera has been disconnected from the system
 * \retval -EACCES The camera is not running so requests can't be queued
 * \retval -EXDEV The request does not belong to this camera
 * \retval -EINVAL The request is invalid
 * \retval -ENOMEM No buffer memory was available to handle the request
 */
int Camera::queueRequest

 * without any ordering constraint.
 *

 */

\brief Start capture from camera
 * \param[in] controls Controls to be applied before starting the Camera
 *
 * Start the camera capture session, optionally providing a list of controls to
 * apply before starting. Once the camera is started the application can queue

 * capture session is terminated with \a stop().

 * synchronized by the caller with other functions that affect the camera
 * state.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -ENODEV The camera has been disconnected from the system
 * \retval -EACCES The camera is not in a state where it can be started
 */

\brief Create a request object for the camera
 * \param[in] cookie Opaque cookie for application use
 *
 * This function creates an empty request for the application to fill with
 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.
 *
 * The \a cookie is stored in the request and is accessible through the
 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.
 *
 * The ownership of the returned request is passed to the caller, which is
 * responsible for deleting it. The request may be deleted in the completion
 * handler, or reused after resetting its state with Request::reuse().
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Configured or Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return A pointer to the newly created request, or nullptr on error
 */
std::unique_ptr<Request> Camera::createRequest(uint64_t cookie)

\brief Start capture from camera
 * \param[in] controls Controls to be applied before starting the Camera
 *
 * Start the camera capture session, optionally providing a list of controls to
 * apply before starting. Once the camera is started the application can queue
 * requests to the camera to process and return to the application until the
 * capture session is terminated with \a stop().
 *
 * \context This function may only be called when the camera is in the
 * Configured state as defined in \ref camera_operation, and shall be
 * synchronized by the caller with other functions that affect the camera
 * state.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -ENODEV The camera has been disconnected from the system
 * \retval -EACCES The camera is not in a state where it can be started
 */
int Camera::start(const ControlList *controls)

\brief Create a request object for the camera
 * \param[in] cookie Opaque cookie for application use
 *
 * This function creates an empty request for the application to fill with
 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.
 *
 * The \a cookie is stored in the request and is accessible through the
 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.
 *
 * The ownership of the returned request is passed to the caller, which is
 * responsible for deleting it. The request may be deleted in the completion
 * handler, or reused after resetting its state with Request::reuse().
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Configured or Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return A pointer to the newly created request, or nullptr on error
 */
std::unique_ptr<Request> Camera::createRequest(uint64_t cookie)

\brief Start capture from camera
 * \param[in] controls Controls to be applied before starting the Camera
 *
 * Start the camera capture session, optionally providing a list of controls to
 * apply before starting. Once the camera is started the application can queue
 * requests to the camera to process and return to the application until the
 * capture session is terminated with \a stop().
 *
 * \context This function may only be called when the camera is in the
 * Configured state as defined in \ref camera_operation, and shall be
 * synchronized by the caller with other functions that affect the camera
 * state.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -ENODEV The camera has been disconnected from the system
 * \retval -EACCES The camera is not in a state where it can be started
 */
int Camera::start(const ControlList *controls)

findings.claim_quote: The pipeline handler must call completeBuffer() and completeRequest() on the CameraManager thread. The same rules as completeRequest() apply to cancelRequest(). When a request is complete, the pipeline handler calls Camera::requestComplete to notify the camera. Camera::requestComplete calls requestCompleted.emit(request) to emit a signal notifying the application of the completed request.

findings.scope: Camera API의 완료 알림 계약과 파이프라인 핸들러의 대기열 처리입니다.

\fn PipelineHandler::queueRequestDevice()
 * \brief Queue a request to the device
 * \param[in] camera The camera to queue the request to
 * \param[in] request The request to queue
 *
 * This function queues a capture request to the device for processing. The
 * request contains a set of buffers associated with streams and a set of
 * parameters. The pipeline handler shall program the device to ensure that the
 * parameters will be applied to the frames captured in the buffers provided in
 * the request.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 */

\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer(Request *request, FrameBuffer *buffer)

findings.claim_quote: Even when the last buffer completes, the request does not complete automatically, so the pipeline handler must explicitly complete the request by calling completeRequest(). After marking the request as complete, completeRequest checks requests starting from the front of queuedRequests_. If the status of the request at the front is RequestPending, the function stops iterating and does not check the requests behind it. Otherwise, the function verifies that no buffers are pending, removes the request from the queue, and calls requestComplete() to return the request to the application in submission order.

\brief Create a request object for the camera
 * \param[in] cookie Opaque cookie for application use
 *
 * This function creates an empty request for the application to fill with
 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.
 *
 * The \a cookie is stored in the request and is accessible through the
 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.
 *
 * The ownership of the returned request is passed to the caller, which is
 * responsible for deleting it. The request may be deleted in the completion
 * handler, or reused after resetting its state with Request::reuse().
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Configured or Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return A pointer to the newly created request, or nullptr on error
 */
std::unique_ptr<Request> Camera::createRequest(uint64_t cookie)

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer(Request *request, FrameBuffer *buffer)
{
	Camera *camera = request->_d()->camera();
	camera->bufferCompleted.emit(request, buffer);
	return request->_d()->completeBuffer(buffer);
}

catalog/cc13337248296521.text: 애플리케이션은 촬영을 준비하기 위해 카메라를 확보하고 구성한 뒤 시작해야 하며, 시작된 카메라는 정지할 때까지 요청을 처리할 수 있고, 애플리케이션은 사용을 마치면 카메라를 해제해야 합니다. 애플리케이션은 카메라를 해제하지 않은 동안 여러 번 시작하고 정지할 수 있으며, 카메라를 재구성할 수도 있습니다. catalog/cc13337248296521/en.text: To prepare for capture, the application must acquire and configure the camera, then start it. Once started, the camera can process requests until it is stopped, and the application must release the camera when it has finished using it. While the camera remains acquired, the application can start and stop it multiple times and can also reconfigure it. The Camera class generally does not synchronize functions that affect the camera state with one another, so the caller must ensure synchronization of these functions when necessary. When an implementer of match for new hardware has acquired all the media devices required for a pipeline, the implementer must create one or more Camera instances, store them internally, and register them with the camera manager.

catalog/8c98cf06e9a737ea.text: 파이프라인 핸들러는 요청의 버퍼 완료를 알리기 위해 CameraManager 스레드에서 completeBuffer()를 호출해야 합니다. 이 함수는 애플리케이션에 버퍼 완료를 통지하고 요청 내부의 버퍼 추적 정보를 갱신합니다. 마지막 버퍼를 완료해도 요청 전체가 자동으로 완료되는 것은 아닙니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeBuffer로 버퍼 완료를 알리고, 요청은 completeRequest를 명시적으로 호출해 완료해야 합니다.

catalog/8c98cf06e9a737ea/en.text: The pipeline handler must call completeBuffer() on the CameraManager thread to signal the completion of a buffer in the request. This function notifies the application that the buffer is complete and updates the buffer tracking information within the request. Completing the last buffer does not automatically complete the entire request. The pipeline handler must signal buffer completion with completeBuffer and explicitly complete the request by calling completeRequest.

catalog/1db2d36b239cc850.text: createIPA 내부 람다는 isSignatureValid(m)이 참이면 T::Threaded 프록시 객체를 생성하고, 거짓이면 T::Isolated 프록시 객체를 생성합니다. createIPA는 생성한 프록시의 isValid 검사가 실패하면 오류를 기록하고 nullptr을 반환합니다. createIPA는 생성한 프록시가 유효성 검사를 통과하면 해당 프록시를 반환합니다.

catalog/1db2d36b239cc850/en.text: The lambda inside createIPA creates a T::Threaded Proxy object if isSignatureValid(m) is true, and a T::Isolated Proxy object if it is false. If the isValid check of the created Proxy fails, createIPA logs an error and returns nullptr. If the created Proxy passes validation, createIPA returns that Proxy.

catalog/3f9cc2d54c6ee372.text: 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeRequest가 반환된 뒤에는 더 이상 관리하지 않는 해당 요청에 접근해서는 안 됩니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 완료된 요청을 순서 제약 없이 completeRequest에 전달할 수 있으며, 이 함수는 요청을 제출 순서대로 애플리케이션에 반환합니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeRequest를 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다.

catalog/3f9cc2d54c6ee372/en.text: The pipeline handler must not access the corresponding request after completeRequest has returned, because the pipeline handler no longer manages it. The pipeline handler can pass completed requests to completeRequest without any ordering constraints, and this function returns the requests to the application in submission order. The pipeline handler must call completeRequest on the CameraManager thread.

catalog/cf09f7c08436100c.text: 애플리케이션은 createRequest()로 할당한 요청을 Camera::queueRequest()에 전달하기 전에 최소 한 개의 캡처 버퍼로 채워야 하며, 버퍼가 없는 요청은 유효하지 않아 큐에 들어가지 않고 거부됩니다. Camera::queueRequest()로 큐에 넣은 요청의 처리가 완료되면 카메라는 requestCompleted 신호로 애플리케이션에 알립니다. 호출자는 카메라가 Running 상태일 때만 Camera::queueRequest()를 호출해야 합니다.

catalog/cf09f7c08436100c/en.text: The application must populate a request allocated with createRequest() with at least one capture buffer before passing it to Camera::queueRequest(). A request without a buffer is invalid and is rejected without being queued. When processing of a request queued with Camera::queueRequest() is complete, the camera notifies the application with the requestCompleted signal. The caller must call Camera::queueRequest() only when the camera is in the Running state.

catalog/1b80b85a4247e633.text: Camera 상태를 바꾸는 함수를 호출하는 호출자는 필요한 경우 함수 간 동기화를 보장해야 합니다. 호출자는 PipelineHandler::completeRequest()를 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다.

catalog/1b80b85a4247e633/en.text: Callers invoking functions that change the Camera state must ensure synchronization between the functions when necessary. Callers must call PipelineHandler::completeRequest() on the CameraManager thread.

catalog/5376f4ccfbc77ab6.text: Camera::start는 isAccessAllowed에 허용 상태 값으로 Private::CameraConfigured를 전달합니다. Camera::start의 호출자는 카메라 상태에 영향을 주는 다른 함수와 이 호출을 동기화해야 합니다. 문서화 대상은 카메라 시작 타이밍입니다.

catalog/5376f4ccfbc77ab6/en.text: Camera::start passes Private::CameraConfigured to isAccessAllowed as the allowed state value. The caller of Camera::start must synchronize this call with other functions that affect the camera state. The timing of camera startup is to be documented.

catalog/3d37fab169d774b1.text: 호출자는 카메라가 Configured 상태일 때만 Camera::start를 호출할 수 있습니다. 카메라 상태에 영향을 주는 함수들은 일반적으로 Camera 클래스에서 서로 동기화하지 않습니다. 호출자는 필요한 경우 이 함수들을 동기화해야 합니다.

catalog/3d37fab169d774b1/en.text: The caller can call Camera::start only when the camera is in the Configured state. Functions that affect the camera state are generally not synchronized with one another in the Camera class. The caller must synchronize these functions when necessary.

catalog/885073788254d1b3.text: Camera::createRequest()는 스레드 안전 함수입니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 스레드 안전 함수입니다. 이 함수는 카메라가 Running 상태일 때만 호출할 수 있습니다. 호출자는 Camera::start와 Camera::stop을 각각 카메라 상태에 영향을 주는 다른 함수와 동기화해야 합니다.

catalog/885073788254d1b3/en.text: Camera::createRequest() is a thread-safe function. Camera::queueRequest() is a thread-safe function. This function can be called only when the camera is in the Running state. The caller must synchronize Camera::start and Camera::stop each with other functions that affect the camera state.

catalog/bae5175c944593b3.text: 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeBuffer()와 completeRequest()를 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다. cancelRequest()에는 completeRequest()와 같은 규칙이 적용됩니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 요청이 완료되면 Camera::requestComplete를 호출해 카메라에 알립니다. Camera::requestComplete는 requestCompleted.emit(request)를 호출해 완료된 요청을 애플리케이션에 알리는 신호를 발행합니다.

catalog/bae5175c944593b3/en.text: The pipeline handler must call completeBuffer() and completeRequest() on the CameraManager thread. The same rules as completeRequest() apply to cancelRequest(). When a request is complete, the pipeline handler calls Camera::requestComplete to notify the camera. Camera::requestComplete calls requestCompleted.emit(request) to emit a signal notifying the application of the completed request.

catalog/0ec721dd2951522e.text: Camera::queueRequest가 0을 반환하면 요청을 큐에 넣는 데 성공했음을 의미합니다. 요청이 큐에 들어간 후 카메라는 requestCompleted 신호로 완료를 알립니다. waitingRequests_는 준비를 기다리는 요청을 보관하며, 맨 앞 요청이 준비되지 않으면 뒤의 요청도 장치로 전달하지 않습니다. maxQueuedRequestsDevice_는 장치에 큐잉된 요청 수의 한도로, queuedRequests_의 크기가 이 값과 같으면 대기 요청의 전달을 중단합니다.

catalog/0ec721dd2951522e/en.text: If Camera::queueRequest returns 0, the request was successfully queued. After the request is queued, the camera signals its completion with requestCompleted. waitingRequests_ holds requests waiting to become ready; if the request at the front is not ready, it does not forward subsequent requests to the device. maxQueuedRequestsDevice_ is the limit on the number of requests queued to the device. If the size of queuedRequests_ equals this value, forwarding of pending requests stops.

catalog/99d6fb26203f2ec8.text: 함수 이름은 PipelineHandler::queueRequestDevice()이며, 성공 시 0을 반환합니다. 오류가 발생하면 음수 오류 코드를 반환합니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 요청의 버퍼 완료를 알리기 위해 CameraManager 스레드에서 completeBuffer()를 호출해야 합니다. 마지막 버퍼가 완료되어도 요청은 자동으로 완료되지 않으므로 completeRequest()를 명시적으로 호출해야 합니다.

catalog/99d6fb26203f2ec8/en.text: The function is named PipelineHandler::queueRequestDevice() and returns 0 on success. If an error occurs, the function returns a negative error code. The pipeline handler must call completeBuffer() on the CameraManager thread to signal completion of a buffer in the request. Even when the last buffer is completed, the request is not completed automatically, so the pipeline handler must explicitly call completeRequest().

catalog/5570030e70a8758a.text: 마지막 버퍼가 완료되어도 요청은 자동으로 완료되지 않으므로, 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeRequest()를 호출하여 요청을 명시적으로 완료해야 합니다. completeRequest는 완료된 요청을 표시한 뒤 queuedRequests_의 맨 앞부터 확인합니다. 맨 앞 요청의 상태가 RequestPending이면 반복을 중단하므로 그 뒤의 요청은 확인하지 않습니다. 그렇지 않으면 대기 중인 버퍼가 없음을 확인하고 해당 요청을 큐에서 제거한 뒤 requestComplete()를 호출하여 애플리케이션에 제출 순서대로 반환합니다.

catalog/5570030e70a8758a/en.text: Even when the last buffer completes, the request does not complete automatically, so the pipeline handler must explicitly complete the request by calling completeRequest(). After marking the request as complete, completeRequest checks requests starting from the front of queuedRequests_. If the status of the request at the front is RequestPending, the function stops iterating and does not check the requests behind it. Otherwise, the function verifies that no buffers are pending, removes the request from the queue, and calls requestComplete() to return the request to the application in submission order.

catalog/17213e255910fe0b.text: Camera::createRequest()가 반환한 요청의 소유권은 호출자에게 넘어가며, 호출자는 요청을 삭제할 책임이 있습니다. 호출자는 완료 핸들러에서 요청을 삭제하거나 Request::reuse()로 상태를 초기화한 뒤 재사용할 수 있습니다. Request::addBuffer()는 요청에 버퍼의 참조를 저장합니다. 호출자는 요청 완료 콜백이 호출될 때까지 버퍼가 유효하게 유지되도록 해야 합니다.

catalog/17213e255910fe0b/en.text: Ownership of the request returned by Camera::createRequest() passes to the caller, who is responsible for deleting it. The caller may delete the request in the completion handler or reset its state with Request::reuse() and reuse it. Request::addBuffer() stores a reference to the buffer in the request. The caller must ensure that the buffer remains valid until the request completion callback is called.

catalog/ffb688343bad5630.text: 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeRequest()를 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 하며, 함수가 반환된 뒤에는 해당 요청에 접근해서는 안 됩니다. 이 함수는 완료된 요청을 순서에 관계없이 호출받을 수 있으며, 요청을 제출 순서대로 애플리케이션에 반환합니다. 조사 계획에서는 호출 문맥과 별도로 대기열 앞 요청의 상태를 확인합니다. 상태가 Request::RequestPending이면 반복문을 빠져나가고, 그렇지 않으면 해당 요청을 대기열에서 꺼내 camera->requestComplete(req)를 호출하는 다음 분기를 확인합니다.

catalog/ffb688343bad5630/en.text: The pipeline handler must call completeRequest() on the CameraManager thread and must not access the request after the function returns. This function may be called with completed requests in any order and returns requests to the application in submission order. The investigation plan checks the status of the request at the front of the queue separately from the calling context. If the status is Request::RequestPending, the loop exits; otherwise, the plan checks the next branch, which removes the request from the queue and calls camera->requestComplete(req).

catalog/0f876f3d920cfff8.text: Camera::queueRequest()는 앞선 카메라 상태, 요청의 생성 카메라, 요청 상태와 제어 목록 검사를 통과한 뒤 request->buffers()가 비어 있으면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 요청의 각 버퍼에 연결된 stream을 activeStreams_.find(stream)으로 찾고, 결과가 activeStreams_.end()와 같으면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 요청을 카메라에 큐잉하는 데 성공하면 0을 반환하며, 이 반환이 촬영 완료를 뜻하지는 않습니다. 요청이 큐잉된 후 카메라는 requestCompleted 신호로 완료를 알립니다.

catalog/0f876f3d920cfff8/en.text: Camera::queueRequest() returns -EINVAL if request->buffers() is empty after passing the preceding checks of the camera state, the camera that created the request, the request state, and the control list. Camera::queueRequest() uses activeStreams_.find(stream) to find the stream associated with each buffer in the request and returns -EINVAL if the result equals activeStreams_.end(). Camera::queueRequest() returns 0 if it successfully queues the request to the camera; this return value does not mean that capture is complete. After the request is queued, the camera signals completion with requestCompleted.

catalog/e9bb20c903920914.text: Request::addBuffer()는 요청에 버퍼의 참조를 저장합니다. 호출자는 요청 완료 콜백이 호출될 때까지 버퍼가 유효하게 유지되도록 해야 합니다. Request::addBuffer()가 성공하면 유효한 Fence의 소유권이 buffer로 이동합니다. Request::addBuffer()가 실패하면 전달받은 fence의 소유권을 가져가지 않고 변경하지 않은 상태로 남깁니다.

catalog/e9bb20c903920914/en.text: Request::addBuffer() stores a reference to the buffer in the request. The caller must ensure that the buffer remains valid until the request completion callback is invoked. If Request::addBuffer() succeeds, ownership of the valid Fence is transferred to buffer. If Request::addBuffer() fails, it does not take ownership of the supplied fence and leaves it unchanged.

catalog/f5cd6c61f3810f88.text: PipelineHandler::registerRequest()는 요청이 생성될 때 호출되며, 파이프라인 핸들러가 해당 요청에 필요한 일회성 초기화를 수행할 기회를 제공합니다. PipelineHandler::registerRequest()가 prepared 신호에 연결한 콜백은 doQueueRequests()를 호출합니다. PipelineHandler::queueRequest는 요청이 가리키는 카메라의 내부 목록 waitingRequests_에 request를 추가합니다. PipelineHandler::queueRequest는 prepare 호출에 시간 인자로 300ms, 즉 300밀리초를 전달합니다.

catalog/f5cd6c61f3810f88/en.text: PipelineHandler::registerRequest() is called when a request is created, giving the pipeline handler an opportunity to perform one-time initialization required for that request. The callback that PipelineHandler::registerRequest() connected to the prepared signal calls doQueueRequests(). PipelineHandler::queueRequest adds request to waitingRequests_, the internal list of the camera referenced by the request. PipelineHandler::queueRequest passes 300ms, or 300 milliseconds, as the time argument in the call to prepare.

catalog/0a44f001a75e1eb3.text: 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeRequest가 반환한 뒤 해당 요청에 접근해서는 안 됩니다. 해당 요청은 더 이상 파이프라인 핸들러가 관리하지 않습니다. completeRequest는 요청이 제출 순서대로 애플리케이션에 반환되도록 합니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 완료된 요청에 대해 순서 제약 없이 completeRequest를 호출할 수 있습니다.

catalog/0a44f001a75e1eb3/en.text: The pipeline handler must not access the request after completeRequest returns. The pipeline handler no longer manages the request. completeRequest ensures that requests are returned to the application in submission order. The pipeline handler may call completeRequest for completed requests without any ordering constraints.

catalog/6d6ccedbcc8325af.text: PipelineHandler::completeRequest()의 while 루프는 큐 맨 앞 요청의 상태가 Request::RequestPending이면 break를 실행해 루프를 중단합니다. PipelineHandler::completeRequest()는 대기 중인 요청을 파이프라인에 큐잉할 수 있도록 마지막에 doQueueRequests(camera)를 호출합니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeBuffer와 completeRequest를 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다. PipelineHandler::cancelRequest()는 먼저 request->_d()->cancel()을 호출한 다음 completeRequest(request)를 호출합니다.

catalog/6d6ccedbcc8325af/en.text: The while loop in PipelineHandler::completeRequest() executes break and exits the loop if the status of the request at the front of the queue is Request::RequestPending. PipelineHandler::completeRequest() calls doQueueRequests(camera) at the end so that pending requests can be queued to the pipeline. The pipeline handler must call completeBuffer and completeRequest on the CameraManager thread. PipelineHandler::cancelRequest() first calls request->_d()->cancel() and then calls completeRequest(request).

catalog/2f99a34f98acbb1e.text: 조사 계획으로, 파이프라인 핸들러가 completeBuffer를 호출할 때 버퍼 완료 알림과 요청의 버퍼 추적 결과를 확인합니다. 반환값이 true이면 요청의 모든 버퍼가 완료된 것이고, false이면 그렇지 않습니다. 마지막 버퍼가 완료되어도 요청은 자동으로 완료되지 않으므로, 파이프라인 핸들러가 completeRequest를 별도로 호출하는지 확인합니다. 두 함수는 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다.

catalog/2f99a34f98acbb1e/en.text: The investigation plan is to check the buffer completion notification and the request's buffer tracking result when the pipeline handler calls completeBuffer. If the function returns true, all buffers in the request are complete; if the function returns false, they are not. Because the request does not complete automatically when the last buffer completes, the plan also checks whether the pipeline handler calls completeRequest separately. Both functions must be called on the CameraManager thread.

catalog/2eace40003f58d25.text: 조건 분기, 반복 횟수와 실제 실행 스레드는 이 호출 목록만으로 확정할 수 없습니다. 가상 호출 후보는 실제 객체에 따라 선택됩니다. 예약 표시는 인자로 전달한 메서드 대상을 뜻하며, 비동기 실행을 보증하지 않습니다. 호출부의 연결 방식과 동기화 계약을 확인해야 합니다.

catalog/2eace40003f58d25/en.text: Conditional branches, repeat counts, and the actual execution thread cannot be determined from this call list alone. Virtual call candidates are selected depending on the actual object. The scheduling marker refers to the method target passed as an argument and does not guarantee asynchronous execution. overview/boundary/synchronization.text:
Functions that affect the camera state as defined below are generally not
 * synchronized with each other by the Camera class. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring their synchronization if necessary.
 *
 * \subsection Camera States

overview/boundary/completion.text:
\brief Signal request completion
 * \param[in] request The request that has completed
 *
 * The pipeline handler shall call this function to notify the \a camera that
 * the request has completed. The request is no longer managed by the pipeline
 * handler and shall not be accessed once this function returns.
 *
 * This function ensures that requests will be returned to the application in
 * submission order, the pipeline handler may call it on any complete request
 * without any ordering constraint.
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 */
void PipelineHandler::completeRequest

vendor-integration/request/completion-co.text:
\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer

camera-model/concurrency/create.text:
\brief Create a request object for the camera
 * \param[in] cookie Opaque cookie for application use
 *
 * This function creates an empty request for the application to fill with
 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.
 *
 * The \a cookie is stored in the request and is accessible through the
 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.
 *
 * The ownership of the returned request is passed to the caller, which is
 * responsible for deleting it. The request may be deleted in the completion
 * handler, or reused after resetting its state with Request::reuse().
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Configured or Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return A pointer to the newly created request, or nullptr on error
 */
std::unique_ptr<Request> Camera::createRequest(uint64_t cookie)

camera-model/concurrency/start.text:
\brief Start capture from camera
 * \param[in] controls Controls to be applied before starting the Camera
 *
 * Start the camera capture session, optionally providing a list of controls to
 * apply before starting. Once the camera is started the application can queue
 * requests to the camera to process and return to the application until the
 * capture session is terminated with \a stop().
 *
 * \context This function may only be called when the camera is in the
 * Configured state as defined in \ref camera_operation, and shall be
 * synchronized by the caller with other functions that affect the camera
 * state.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -ENODEV The camera has been disconnected from the system
 * \retval -EACCES The camera is not in a state where it can be started
 */
int Camera::start(const ControlList *controls)

vendor-integration/boundary/repeat.text:
\fn PipelineHandler::match(DeviceEnumerator *enumerator)
 * \brief Match media devices and create camera instances
 * \param[in] enumerator The enumerator providing all media devices found in the
 * system
 *
 * This function is the main entry point of the pipeline handler. It is called
 * by the camera manager with the \a enumerator passed as an argument. It shall
 * acquire from the \a enumerator all the media devices it needs for a single
 * pipeline, create one or multiple Camera instances and register them with the
 * camera manager.
 *
 * If all media devices needed by the pipeline handler are found, they must all
 * be acquired by a call to MediaDevice::acquire(). This function shall then
 * create the corresponding Camera instances, store them internally, and return
 * true. Otherwise it shall not acquire any media device (or shall release all
 * the media devices is has acquired by calling MediaDevice::release()) and
 * return false.
 *
 * If multiple instances of a pipeline are available in the system, the
 * PipelineHandler class will be instantiated once per instance, and its match()
 * function called for every instance. Each call shall acquire media devices for
 * one pipeline instance, until all compatible media devices are exhausted.
 *
 * If this function returns true, a new instance of the pipeline handler will
 * be created and its match() function called.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return true if media devices have been acquired and camera instances
 * created, or false otherwise
 */

vendor-integration/configuration/generat.text:
\fn PipelineHandler::generateConfiguration()
 * \brief Generate a camera configuration for a specified camera
 * \param[in] camera The camera to generate a default configuration for
 * \param[in] roles A list of stream roles
 *
 * Generate a default configuration for the \a camera for a specified list of
 * stream roles. The caller shall populate the \a roles with the use-cases it
 * wishes to fetch the default configuration for. The returned configuration
 * can then be examined by the caller to learn about the selected streams and
 * their default parameters.
 *
 * The intended companion to this is \a configure() which can be used to change
 * the group of streams parameters.
 *
 * \context This function may be called from any thread and shall be
 * \threadsafe. It shall not modify the state of the \a camera in the pipeline
 * handler.
 *
 * \return A valid CameraConfiguration if the requested roles can be satisfied,
 * or a null pointer otherwise.

\fn PipelineHandler::configure()
 * \brief Configure a group of streams for capture
 * \param[in] camera The camera to configure
 * \param[in] config The camera configurations to setup
 *
 * Configure the specified group of streams for \a camera according to the
 * configuration specified in \a config. The intended caller of this interface
 * is the Camera class which will receive configuration to apply from the
 * application.
 *
 * The configuration is guaranteed to have been validated with
 * CameraConfiguration::validate(). The pipeline handler implementation shall
 * not perform further validation and may rely on any custom field stored in its
 * custom CameraConfiguration derived class.
 *
 * When configuring the camera the pipeline handler shall associate a Stream
 * instance to each StreamConfiguration entry in the CameraConfiguration using
 * the StreamConfiguration::setStream() function.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 */

overview/request/queue.text:
\brief Queue a request to the camera
 * \param[in] request The request to queue to the camera
 *
 * This function queues a \a request to the camera for capture.
 *
 * After allocating the request with createRequest(), the application shall
 * fill it with at least one capture buffer before queuing it. Requests that
 * contain no buffers are invalid and are rejected without being queued.
 *
 * Once the request has been queued, the camera will notify its completion
 * through the \ref requestCompleted signal.
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -ENODEV The camera has been disconnected from the system
 * \retval -EACCES The camera is not running so requests can't be queued
 * \retval -EXDEV The request does not belong to this camera
 * \retval -EINVAL The request is invalid
 * \retval -ENOMEM No buffer memory was available to handle the request
 */
int Camera::queueRequest

 * \param[in] controls Controls to be applied before starting the Camera
 *
 * Start the camera capture session, optionally providing a list of controls to
 * apply before starting. Once the camera is started the application can queue
 * requests to the camera to process and return to the application until the
 * capture session is terminated with \a stop().
 *
 * \context This function may only be called when the camera is in the
 * Configured state as defined in \ref camera_operation, and shall be
 * synchronized by the caller with other functions that affect the camera
 * state.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -ENODEV The camera has been disconnected from the system
 * \retval -EACCES The camera is not in a state where it can be started
 */
int Camera::start

request-lifecycle/journey/buffer-notice.text:
\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer(Request *request, FrameBuffer *buffer)

request-lifecycle/resources/buffer-duty.text:
\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

pipeline-requests/completion/buffer-cont.text:
\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer(Request *request, FrameBuffer *buffer)
{
	Camera *camera = request->_d()->camera();
	camera->bufferCompleted.emit(request, buffer);
	return request->_d()->completeBuffer(buffer);
}

vendor-integration/integration/camera.text:
An application needs to perform a sequence of operations on a camera before
 * it is ready to process requests. The camera needs to be acquired and
 * configured to prepare the camera for capture. Once started the camera can
 * process requests until it is stopped. When an application is done with a
 * camera, the camera needs to be released.

vendor-integration/integration/restart.text:
An application may start and stop a camera multiple times as long as it is
 * not released. The camera may also be reconfigured.
